Network Comparison Test

Source: R/nct.R
nct.Rd

Tests whether two networks estimated from independent samples differ at three levels (van Borkulo et al. 2022): network structure (M-statistic, the largest absolute edge difference), global strength (S-statistic, the difference in summed absolute edge weights; with abs = FALSE, summed signed weights, i.e. global expected influence), and individual edges (E-statistic per edge). Inference is via permutation of group labels.

Usage

nct(
  data1,
  data2,
  iter = 1000L,
  gamma = 0.5,
  paired = FALSE,
  abs = TRUE,
  weighted = TRUE,
  p_adjust = "none",
  na_method = c("pairwise", "listwise")
)

# S3 method for class 'net_nct'
print(x, n = Inf, ...)

# S3 method for class 'net_nct'
summary(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'net_nct'
as.data.frame(x, row.names = NULL, optional = FALSE, ...)

Arguments

data1

A numeric matrix or data.frame of observations from group 1.

data2

A numeric matrix or data.frame of observations from group 2, with the same variables as data1.

iter

Integer. Number of permutation iterations. Default 1000.

gamma

EBIC tuning parameter for glasso. Default 0.5.

paired

Logical. If TRUE, perform a paired permutation (within-subject swap; row i of both groups is the same unit). Default FALSE.

abs

Logical. If TRUE, compute global strength on absolute edge weights. Default TRUE.

weighted

Logical. If TRUE, use weighted networks for the tests. If FALSE, binarize before computing statistics. Default TRUE.

p_adjust

P-value adjustment method for the per-edge tests (any method in stats::p.adjust.methods). Default "none".

na_method

"pairwise" (default) or "listwise" handling of missing values; see Details.

x

For the print() and as.data.frame() methods: an object of class net_nct.

n

For the print() method: number of edges to list, largest difference first. Default Inf (all).

...

In print.net_nct(), summary.net_nct() and as.data.frame.net_nct(): Ignored.

object

For the summary() method: an object of class net_nct.

row.names, optional

For as.data.frame(): ignored (base generic compatibility).

Value

A list of class net_nct with elements:

nw1, nw2

Estimated weighted adjacency matrices.

structure

The network-structure test (statistic M, the largest absolute edge difference): list with observed, perm, p_value. P-values are permutation p-values, (sum(perm >= observed) + 1) / (iter + 1).

strength

The global-strength test (statistic S): same structure, plus by_group, each network's global strength (NCT's glstrinv.sep).

E

Same structure for the per-edge tests (observed and p_value are one value per upper-triangle edge, perm an iter by edges matrix), plus edge_names, a data frame with columns from and to naming each node pair.

n_iter

Number of permutations.

groups

Display names of the two groups: the argument names when they are plain variables, otherwise "group 1" / "group 2".

n

Rows used in each group.

paired

Whether a paired test was used.

params

List of the settings used: gamma, abs, weighted, p_adjust, na_method.

The letters follow van Borkulo et al. (2022) and NetworkComparisonTest. Before Nestimate 0.9.27 the fields $M and $S held the global-strength and network-structure tests the other way round; accessing them now raises a nestimate_renamed error. Errors of class nestimate_bad_input for malformed arguments or groups whose columns differ (in name or order); of class nestimate_degenerate_sample when (pairwise) a variable pair shares fewer than two observed rows in a group or a permuted split. A warning of class nestimate_constant_variable when a variable is constant in an observed group.

In print.net_nct(): The input object, invisibly.

In summary.net_nct(): a data frame with one row per global test, columns test ("network structure"; "global strength", or "global expected influence" when abs = FALSE), statistic ("M", "S"), observed, p_value, significant (p_value < 0.05).

In as.data.frame.net_nct(): a data frame with one row per node pair, columns from, to, weight_1, weight_2 (the edge in each group's network), difference (statistic E), p_value, significant.

Details

Follows NetworkComparisonTest::NCT() with defaults abs = TRUE, weighted = TRUE, paired = FALSE. The network estimator is EBIC-selected glasso (psychnets::ebic_glasso()) applied to a Pearson correlation matrix, with Matrix::nearPD symmetrization (matching NCT's NCT_estimator_GGM default). Under the same seed both functions permute the same rows, so permutation p-values agree; the glasso solver is not the Fortran one NCT wraps, so the test statistics agree to independent-solver precision (of the order of 1e-4) rather than bit-for-bit.

The two groups must hold the same variables in the same order (non-numeric columns such as an id or a group label are dropped first).

Missing data follow na_method. "pairwise" (default) keeps every row, permutes rows as usual, and estimates each (sub)sample from its pairwise-complete correlation matrix, with the median pairwise co-observation count as the sample size. "listwise" drops incomplete rows first (in a paired design, a pair is dropped when either member is incomplete). Complete data are unaffected by the choice.

A variable without variation in a group, or in a permuted split (a rare binary item can be constant in a split), enters that network as an isolated node. The statistic is then defined on every split, so the permutation test stays exact. A constant variable in an observed group raises a nestimate_constant_variable warning.

Methods

  • Printing the object shows every result. summary.net_nct() returns the M (network structure) and S (global strength) tests; as.data.frame.net_nct() returns one row per edge.

References

van Borkulo, C. D., van Bork, R., Boschloo, L., Kossakowski, J. J., Tio, P., Schoevers, R. A., Borsboom, D., & Waldorp, L. J. (2022). Comparing network structures on three aspects: A permutation test. Psychological Methods. doi:10.1037/met0000476

Examples

set.seed(1)
x1 <- matrix(rnorm(100 * 4), 100, 4)
x2 <- matrix(rnorm(100 * 4), 100, 4)
colnames(x1) <- colnames(x2) <- paste0("V", 1:4)
# iter = 20 keeps the example fast; a real analysis uses 1000 or more.
res <- nct(x1, x2, iter = 20)
res
#> Network Comparison Test: x1 vs x2
#> 20 permutations, independent groups, n = 100 and 100
#> 
#>   Test                  Statistic       p
#>   M  network structure      0.000   1.000 
#>   S  global strength        0.000   1.000 
#>        x1 0.000 vs x2 0.000
#>   E  edges differing       0 of 6
#> 
#>   Edges, largest difference first
#>   Edge         x1      x2  |diff|       p
#>   V1 - V2   0.000   0.000   0.000   1.000 
#>   V1 - V3   0.000   0.000   0.000   1.000 
#>   V1 - V4   0.000   0.000   0.000   1.000 
#>   V2 - V3   0.000   0.000   0.000   1.000 
#>   V2 - V4   0.000   0.000   0.000   1.000 
#>   V3 - V4   0.000   0.000   0.000   1.000 
#> 
#>   * p < 0.05
summary(res)
#>                test statistic observed p_value significant
#> 1 network structure         M        0       1       FALSE
#> 2   global strength         S        0       1       FALSE
